section: Educational Psychology · Ch14 — Three Types of Guidance (Complete)
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A school counsellor helps a struggling Class 9 student choose between continuing with Science or switching to Humanities, based on the student's academic strengths and interests, and advises on study techniques to improve performance. This is an example of:
explanation: Educational guidance helps students with academic decisions — subject/stream choice, study habits, and adjusting to school life — distinct from vocational guidance (career choice after schooling) and personal guidance (emotional/social difficulties).

section: Educational Psychology · Ch14 — Three Types of Guidance (Complete)
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A teacher notices a student is withdrawn and having difficulty making friends after moving to a new school, and arranges supportive conversations to help the student adjust socially and emotionally. This is an example of:
explanation: Personal (or personal-social) guidance addresses emotional, social and adjustment difficulties — helping students cope with relationships, self-esteem and personal problems — distinct from academic (educational) or career-related (vocational) guidance.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch14 — Three Types of Guidance (Complete)
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Guidance services in schools are traditionally classified into three broad types. Which of the following correctly lists all three?
explanation: The classic three-fold classification of school guidance is Educational (academic decisions), Vocational (career choices), and Personal/Personal-Social (emotional and social adjustment) — a foundational categorisation in guidance and counselling.
